summary: The applied-polearm reach path reaches uhitm.c:attack_checks() before hit resolution. C passes the current ParanoidHit Boolean, false for this session, so the recorded y confirms the peaceful target. JavaScript passes the PARANOID_HIT bit mask itself, making the query always require the word yes; y remains unconsumed and the attack never reaches thitmonst() or hmon(). The whole-function divergence scope is attack_checks() in uhitm.c; apply.c:use_pole() and the downstream hmon path are present in the examined snapshot.

source.branch: In attack_checks(), when flags.confirm is enabled and the spotted target is peaceful, while the hero is not confused, hallucinating, or stunned, the ParanoidHit Boolean controls whether paranoid_query() accepts the single key y or requires yes. The JavaScript caller currently supplies PARANOID_HIT, the nonzero mask, instead of testing the current paranoia_bits value.
dependencies: options.c:initoptions():7173; the default mask contains pray, swim, and trap, not hit
do_name.c:mon_nam(), used to construct the peaceful-target prompt

evidence: The assigned diagnostic .cache/synthetic-scans/v15/samurai-polearm-hits-reach-target.json reports the first screen mismatch at segment 0, step 62, key ".": C cell column 25 is "n" and JavaScript is "e"; C cursor is column 32 and JavaScript column 35. The recorded C screen is "Really attack the orc? [yn] (n)". A one-case in-memory replay of the assigned recording at the examined commit shows JavaScript "Really attack the orc? [yes|n] (n)" at step 62 and the same prompt with a trailing " y" at step 63.

The C recording challenges/cases/v15/samurai-polearm-hits-reach-target.session.json has step 63 key "y" and emits "You dishonorably attack the innocent! The naginata hits the orc." Its final-step RNG calls include gethungry(eat.c:3191), rnd(20) in thitmonst(dothrow.c:2152), and rnd(6) in dmgval(weapon.c:265). The one-case JavaScript replay remains at RNG count 2881 through step 63, confirming it never consumes that answer or enters hit resolution.

Upstream src/uhitm.c:308-323 passes ParanoidHit to paranoid_query() for the peaceful-target confirmation. Upstream include/flag.h:564 defines ParanoidHit as a Boolean membership test on flags.paranoia_bits; options.c:initoptions():7173 initializes defaults without PARANOID_HIT. In the pinned JavaScript, js/uhitm.js:945-949 passes PARANOID_HIT itself. Its nonzero value makes js/cmd.js:901-948 select the line-based "yes" prompt, which leaves the recorded single-key y in the input stream. The divergence is in the attack_checks() confirmation branch, so scope the correction to that existing whole source function.

The session reaches upstream src/apply.c:use_pole():3426-3557 through doapply():4407-4411; use_pole() calls attack_checks() at 3493 before thitmonst() at 3521. Upstream dothrow.c:2011-2209 sets HMON_APPLIED when the wielded polearm is used and calls hmon(); the pinned JavaScript wires the same route in js/apply.js:947-1057 and js/dothrow.js:2714-2917. js/uhitm.js:1539-1563 implements hmon(), so hmon support exists but is not reached while the confirmation input remains pending.
